We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 3 reactions, using templates ['324324', '1914396', '733'] in this order.

We have applied 324324 to target, got two fragments: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1" and "Nc1ccccc1N". So first disconnection splits the amide (C=O)N? Actually original had C(=O)N attached to phenyl amine. The template gave product with carboxylic acid (C=O)O and an aniline (Nc1ccccc1N). Good.

Second step: apply 1914396 to the first fragment (the sulfonyl phenyl with carboxylic acid). It gave "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" and "O=C(O)CC(=O)O". So it broke the double bond? Actually gave aldehyde (C=O) on second phenyl and a dicarboxylic acid (oxalic acid? O=C(O)CC(=O)O). So second disconnection yields an aldehyde phenyl sulfonyl and a dicarboxylic acid.

Third step: apply template 733 to the aldehyde phenyl sulfonyl? Template 733 is a sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and aniline. It transforms sulfonyl chloride + aniline to sulfonamide. Retro direction: from sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride + aniline. Our fragment "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" is a sulfonamide linking two phenyls, one with methyl, other with aldehyde. Applying 733 should give "Cl-[S(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(C=O)cc2]" and "NH2-aryl (the methyl phenyl)". Let's apply.
